chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes there is a dispute between two men from our companions, and they agree on one of us as an arbitrator.' He said: 'That is not it; rather, it is the one who compels people to his ruling by the sword and the whip.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between an arbitrator and a judge in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between a simple arbitrator chosen by mutual consent of disputing parties and a true judge or ruler who has the authority to compel obedience through force (sword and whip). This highlights the distinction between voluntary arbitration and authoritative judicial governance. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is pivotal in defining the scope of *al-Qadi al-Adl* (the just judge) whose ruling is binding (*mujbir*) by divine authority, contrasting with *al-Hakam* whose authority is derived from the parties' agreement.
